check_events.outcome: For this check only, interpret the doubtful dash/arrow as the unit map. The calculation uses g as an abstract morphism name; the transcription retains q/g from the ink. Restricted to an abelian sheaf F and a bounded-below injective resolution I on Y. Assume each injective I^n has injective g^*I^n and epimorphic unit I^n→g_*g^*I^n. Exactness of g^* makes g^*I an injective resolution of g^*F, and the exact left adjoint g^* implies g_* preserves injectives. For K=ker(I→g_*g^*I), the degreewise short exact sequence 0→K→I→g_*g^*I→0 yields K→F→Rg_*g^*F→K[1]. Thus RΓ_Y(K) is the relative fibre model in this restricted case; no additional [-1] is needed on this kernel. This checks the kernel placement, not a functorial choice on bare derived categories, the open-inclusion example, or an unbounded extension.

Elementary check of nonuniqueness only: over a field k, let X=k[-1], Y=k and f=0, so Cone(f)=Y⊕X[1]=k⊕k. The maps (y,x)↦(y+a x,x), for a=0 and a=1, are distinct automorphisms of the cone. Both preserve the inclusion Y→Cone(f) and projection Cone(f)→X[1], hence complete the same identity square on f to maps of its triangle. The commutation is verified directly on (y,x). This proves that a commuting square alone does not determine a unique cone map. It is not a proof that no possible global choice of cone functor can ever be made, and it does not answer the author’s special-case functoriality question.
